discoveryContext: Found on November 23, 2026 while triaging the Wiz blog in the market-feed watcher (PR #243). Wiz Research's report was read the same day; text below is paraphrased. No GitHub statement was fetched.

candidates.title: Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens used to plant secret-dumping workflows across 850+ accounts

discovery.usageRights: Citation and short paraphrase only; check publisher terms before reuse.

candidates.dedupeCheck: No seed incident or candidate shares this identity. Wiz distinguishes Gheist from GhostAction (incident:ghostaction-wave-oct-2026) and says some tokens came from earlier supply-chain compromises such as the March Trivy compromise (see incident:litellm-pypi-trivy-2026). Wiz also reports overlap with the May Megalodon wave, which isn't in the seed.

claims.statement: Wiz Research reports that since September 15, 2026 an automated campaign it calls Gheist used compromised GitHub tokens to push a workflow to every repository those tokens could reach. The workflow printed repository and environment secrets into workflow logs in encoded form; the operator downloaded the logs through the GitHub API and deleted the runs.

Wiz counts more than 850 compromised accounts and more than 13,500 planted branches, from personal projects to enterprise private repositories. It says the tokens likely came from infostealer logs and earlier supply-chain compromises.

Wiz reports follow-on activity in some cases: cloning private repositories, enumerating AWS Secrets Manager with harvested cloud credentials, renaming repositories as cracked-software lures, and abusing GitHub Actions for compute. It says recent GitHub security changes significantly disrupted the campaign.

unresolvedQuestions: Only one source, the researcher who found it. No GitHub statement on the disruption or affected-account count was fetched.
